headline: Global growth holds, but U.S. business needs fixing

drivers.explanation: Company attributes the increase to positive comparable sales in every segment; U.S. growth was driven by favorable product mix, partly offset by fewer guest visits.
Growth included $52M of pre-tax restructuring charges tied to the Company's Accelerating the Organization initiative; excluding those and last year's $43M charge, growth would be one point higher.
Net income growth mirrors operating income: the current quarter absorbed $52M of pre-tax restructuring charges versus $43M a year ago, both tied to Accelerating the Organization.
EPS growth reflects the same revenue and margin drivers; excluding $0.06 per share of restructuring charges this quarter, non-GAAP diluted EPS was $3.38, also up 6%.
Results excluding restructuring charges were driven by higher sales-driven franchised margins and higher other operating income, partly offset by higher selling, general and administrative expenses.

summary_short: Revenue rose to $7,099M (+3.7% y/y, +8.9% q/q) and diluted EPS increased to $3.32 (+5.7% y/y, +19.4% q/q), while comparable sales grew 1.3% globally amid a leadership change in the U.S. business.
summary_long: Revenue reached $7,099M, up 3.7% y/y and 8.9% q/q, as comparable sales rose 1.3% globally (U.S. +0.8%, International Operated +1.5%, Developmental Licensed +1.9%). Operating income grew to $3,338M (+3.3% y/y) despite $52M of restructuring charges tied to Accelerating the Organization; excluding charges, operating income and diluted EPS both would have grown one point faster. Diluted EPS rose to $3.32 (+5.7% y/y, +19.4% q/q; $3.38 non-GAAP). Net income was $2,362M (+4.8% y/y). Cash fell to $822M (-56.2% y/y) while long-term debt eased to $39,863M and the shareholders' deficit narrowed to -$1,023M. No new guidance was issued; McDonald's named a new President of McDonald's USA effective the same day.
